subject: paper:hvolby-2015-sleep
quote: The relationships of ADHD with sleep problems, psychiatric comorbidities and medications are complex and multidirectional.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). States the relationship is multidirectional, not a one-way mimic — the premise of the bidirectional hypothesis. (A separate Hvolby quote already supports the rival-boundary hypothesis in the arousal note.)

subject: paper:bijlenga-2019
quote: ADHD is either the cause or the consequence of sleep disturbances, or they may have a shared etiological and genetic background.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Names all three directions explicitly — cause, consequence, shared background — the core of both the bidirectional hypothesis and the sleep tension.

subject: paper:van-veen-2010
quote: These findings demonstrate diurnal rhythm deviations during everyday life in the majority of adults with ADHD that have SOI
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; SOI = sleep-onset insomnia. Objective actigraphy/melatonin evidence of circadian phase delay in most adult ADHD+insomnia — the empirical basis for the intrinsic-delay reading.

subject: paper:bijlenga-2019
quote: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is highly associated with the delayed sleep phase disorder, a circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder, which is prevalent in 73-78% of children and adults with ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Puts a prevalence figure on delayed sleep phase in ADHD — high enough that it is hard to dismiss as incidental comorbidity.

subject: paper:bijlenga-2019
quote: We propose a novel view on ADHD, where a part of the ADHD symptoms are the result of chronic sleep disorders, with most evidence for the delayed circadian rhythm as the underlying mechanism.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Names delayed circadian rhythm as a proposed underlying mechanism for part of ADHD; medium because it is an explicit proposal ('we propose'), not a settled finding.
